headline: Steady top line, thinner margins, stronger cash flow

kpis.label: Non-IFRS adjusted profit from operations margin

summary_short: Revenue was flat y/y at $614.4M, within Globant's guided range, while non-IFRS adjusted operating margin fell to 13.2% (from 15.0%) and adjusted diluted EPS fell 8.5% to $1.40; free cash flow jumped to $12.6M from -$2.9M a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue was essentially flat y/y at $614.4M, within Globant's guided range. Non-IFRS adjusted operating margin fell to 13.2% (from 15.0%) and adjusted diluted EPS fell 8.5% to $1.40, driven by $32.3M of business-optimization costs from a restructuring during the quarter; IFRS operating margin still rose to 3.2% from 1.0%. Headcount fell 8.9% y/y to 27,411. Free cash flow reached $12.6M versus -$2.9M a year ago. Glob.AI ARR hit $52.8M, up 61% q/q, with management now guiding to at least $110M by year-end. Globant guides FY2026 revenue to $2,428-2,462M and adjusted diluted EPS to $5.75-6.15 — both below the ranges issued with Q1 results. Cash and short-term investments were $168.8M.

Globant reports under IFRS (foreign private issuer, Luxembourg-domiciled, files Form 6-K/20-F), not US GAAP — 'IFRS' and 'Non-IFRS Adjusted' are two distinct company-defined bases in this filing and are kept as separate KPI rows rather than conflated, per the same-basis discipline. The resolver's own eps_usd KPI join mixes bases: its actual (1.40) is Non-IFRS Adjusted Diluted EPS but its prior_yy (-0.05) is IFRS Diluted EPS for Q2 2025 (Non-IFRS Adjusted Diluted EPS for that quarter was actually $1.53 per this release) — this summary bypasses that shard join and instead uses the release's own same-quarter, same-basis comparison table directly for both EPS rows. FY2026 guidance issued in this release ($2,428-2,462M revenue; 13.5%-14.5% adjusted operating margin; $5.75-6.15 adjusted diluted EPS) sits below the FY2026 range Globant issued with Q1 2026 results ($2,462-2,508M revenue; 14%-15% margin; $6.10-6.50 EPS, per the shard's Q1-event guidance entries) — a de facto reduction, but the release itself never uses language such as 'lowering' or 'revising down,' so guidance.move is recorded as null per the explicit-language rule rather than inferred as 'cut.' Revenue and margin guidance also bake in company-disclosed one-time FX tailwinds (+25bps for Q3, +70bps for FY2026).

drivers.explanation: Release states revenue of $614.4M landed within the guided $610-616M range; company attributes account strength to a 6.9% y/y increase in top-50-client revenue and growing adoption of AI Pods and the Glob.AI platform.

drivers.metric: Non-IFRS adjusted profit from operations margin
drivers.explanation: CFO says the company "proactively optimized our structure during the quarter" amid market volatility; the $32.3M of one-off business-optimization costs is the disclosed driver of the adjusted-margin and adjusted-EPS declines.
Same $32.3M business-optimization charge and softer adjusted operating margin flow through to adjusted diluted EPS; not separately explained beyond the margin driver above.
IFRS margin improved y/y because one-off business-optimization costs were $32.3M this quarter versus $47.6M in Q2 2025 — a smaller drag on the unadjusted result even as the adjusted margin fell.
Headcount fell to 27,411 from 30,084 a year ago as part of the same structural-optimization program cited for the margin declines; no separate reason given for headcount specifically.
Not separately explained beyond the release's own comparison to a year-ago quarter of -$2.9 million; management called it the strongest first-half cash generation on record.

CFO Juan Urthiague described the quarter as "resilient execution"; CEO Martín Migoya highlighted Glob.AI ARR up 61% q/q to $52.8M and said the company now expects "no less than $110 million exiting 2026."
